To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interference term in the breakup of a loosely bound halo nucleus is dependent on the beam energy and can have a large contribution in certain angular ranges of the breakup fragments and the breakup of $11\mathrm{Be}$ is a good probe to study the beam energy dependent Coulomb-nuclear interaction.

the beam energy dependence and the angular and energy dependence of Coulmb-nuclear interferences in breakup of halo nuclei are important and should be taken into account in the analysis of experimental data.

the Coulomb and nuclear breakup amplitudes are not independent but they are coupled to each other through the Coulomb-nucleus interference terms which can be as big or even bigger as compared to the individual Coulomb and nuclear terms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the beam energy dependence on Coulomb-nuclear Interference terms in the breakup reaction of $^{11}{\mathrm{Be}}$ on a $^{44}{\mathrm{Ti}}$ target.

the study of the Coulomb and nuclear breakup terms of $^{11}$Be and their interference effects on a medium mass target and the comparison of the breakup cross section on a heavy target with experimental data.
the breakup of exotic halo nuclei on heavy targets at intermediate energies and the role of Coulomb-nucler interference terms therein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the breakup reaction is a very complicated process and the breakup observables can be understood only if all the terms, i.e. Coulomb, nuclear and Coulomb-nuclear, are treated consistently and simultaneously.
the Coulomb effects can not be ignored in the description of the breakup of $^ {11}\mathrm{ Be}$ on a $^{44}\text{Ti}$ target at beam energy as low as 69 MeV/u. S. Mukhopad
the Coulomb and nuclear terms as well as the Coulomb-nucleon interference terms are all important for a complete understanding of the breakup process of $^{11}Be$ on $^{208}Pb$ at 69 Mev/nucleon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Coulomb breakup of $^{12}$Be on a heavy target at a beam energy of 69 MeV is dominated by the nuclear term and the interference term is comparable with the nuclear term.
the Coulomb and nuclear terms are equally important and should be treated consistently to obtain a good description of the breakup of $^11\mathrm{Be}$.
the Coulomb and nuclear terms in the breakup reaction of $^{11}$Be are comparable in size and can not be ignored.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Coulomb breakup calculations are not only dependent on the beam energy but also the target mass and the breakup fragments energy and angle.
the Coulomb and nuclear breakup terms are not additive and their interference terms should not be neglected.
a careful treatment of the breakup process is necessary to obtain accurate predictions of the breakup data.
